critical_flags.justification: The preamble line \renewcommand{\texttt}[1]{\path{#1}} makes \path print pandoc's escape backslashes literally, so the compiled PDF shows the abstract's headline claim as 'f(48)\=\8 and f(49)\=\7', Theorem B as 'BinarySquareRegularExclusion\→\¬\Erdos85Question' and the finite-drop hypothesis as 'hno49\:\¬\C4FreeMinDegreeWitness\49\7' (96 '\_' and 23 '\=' / '\→' / '\¬' artefacts in the pdftotext output). The statements as printed are not the statements the paper makes; a reader cannot take page 1 seriously. Analogue of the vision rubric's mathtext_artifact_breaks_meaning; outside the mechanical render gate's detector set, so set from a direct read of the PDF text.

Section 'A cheaper route' states '1,159 UNSAT verdicts needed 2,695 Kissat core-hours' for the residual whole-instance rows, while the evidence-levels table (L83), the abstract (L35), section 8 (L313, L319) and refs/CENSUS.md all give 1,160 whole-instance two-solver UNSAT rows. For a paper whose Result A is a census count with an 'empty open list', an unexplained off-by-one in the headline count is disqualifying until reconciled (one sentence naming a row without a timing record would suffice, if that is the cause).
